key_insight: A foundation model-based MIL pipeline, especially Athena, generalized best across five countries for detecting high-grade cervical lesions on H&E whole-slide images.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help standardize cervical biopsy screening by improving HSIL detection sensitivity while keeping specificity comparable to trained pathologists.
method: Compared five foundation pathology models: Athena, H-optimus-0, Hibou-L, Midnight-12k, and Virchow.
Evaluated binary HSIL detection on H&E whole-slide images from Portugal, Cambodia, Germany, Poland, and Scotland.
Compared model performance with trained pathologists on a p16-confirmed ground-truth dataset.
evidence_signal: Athena achieved the top mean AUC of 0.931 with the lowest cross-country variability (STD 0.022), and improved sensitivity from 84% to 95% with similar specificity (85% vs 84%).
watch_item: Performance was strongest at the HSIL boundary, so real-world use may still require careful validation for borderline low-grade versus high-grade cases.
paper_title: Cross-country generalizability of foundation models for cervical cancer screenings on H&E whole slide images
